newsitem.title: USA: MMS auction opens with active shallow water bids.
newsitem.headline: MMS auction opens with active shallow water bids.

text.p: The latest auction of drilling rights on offshore Gulf of Mexico tracts opened Wednesday with heated bidding on shallow acreage in federal waters off the coast of Louisiana.

Nine bidders emerged for each of two tracts on the shelf, and several multi-million dollar bids were fielded early in the day-long sale by auctioneer Chris Oynes, regional director of the U.S. Minerals Management Service.

Before unsealing the first of a record 1,790 bids received in the central Gulf lease sale, Oynes donned a red sports jacket -- last used in the early 1980s to signal that the auctioneer "smelled big money" in the auction.
"It looks like we are going to have a lot of money," Oynes said, drawing cheers from a packed New Orleans hotel ballroom.

Although deepwater tracts were the prime attraction in the lease sale, producers submitted bids on 445 tracts in waters less than 400 metres (1,312 feet) deep, according to the MMS, an agency of the Department of the Interior which regulates oil and gas production offshore.
"Those people that said the Gulf was a dead sea not so long ago I think were wrong," said Bob Armstrong, an assistant secretary with the U.S. Department of Interior.

In the lease sale, considered a barometer of drilling activity in the Gulf and the health of the domestic oil and gas industry, producers submit sealed bids on rights to drill in a specified tract in the Gulf. Additional payments, known as royalties, are also paid on oil and gas lifted from the leaseholdings.
A lower royalty rate on deepwater tracts sparked active bidding in waters 800 metres (2,625 feet) or deeper, with producers bidding on 587 tracts eligible for royalty relief.

Barrett Resources, expanding from its core operations as a Rocky Mountain gas producer, again emerged as an active bidder in shallow and deepwater tracts. The company has earmarked $120 million for Gulf drilling this year, a company executive said.
As expected, Norcen Explorer also was actively bidding, building up its inventory of leases after locking up rights to a semisubmersible drilling rig this year.
